# Business Requirements Document — Identity Service (token rotation)

Project: **Identity Service** (code IDN) · Team: Platform · Department: Engineering
Scope of this BRD: **refresh-token rotation and session revocation**. Login,
password reset and SSO federation are already live and out of scope.

## Overview
Every Indnord application signs users in through the Identity Service and
receives a short-lived access token plus a long-lived refresh token. Refresh
tokens today live for 30 days and are reusable, so a stolen refresh token
gives an attacker a month of silent access. This slice makes refresh tokens
single-use, detects reuse, and lets a user or an administrator end sessions.

## Goals
- A leaked refresh token is useless after its first use.
- Reuse of an already-rotated token ends the whole session family within
  one request.
- A user can see and end their own sessions; an admin can end anyone's.

## Users
- **End user**: signs in, keeps using apps without re-login, reviews and
  ends their sessions.
- **Client application**: exchanges a refresh token for a new pair.
- **Security admin**: revokes a user's sessions after an incident.

## Functional requirements

1. **Token pair issue**
   - On sign-in the service issues an access token (15 minutes) and a
     refresh token (30 days) and records a **session** with device label,
     IP, created time and last-used time.
   - Refresh tokens are opaque random strings of at least 256 bits; only a
     hash is stored.

2. **Rotation**
   - Exchanging a refresh token returns a new access token and a **new**
     refresh token, and marks the presented token as used.
   - The new token belongs to the same session (the session id is stable
     across rotations).
   - The last-used time on the session is updated on every exchange.

3. **Reuse detection**
   - Presenting a refresh token that was already rotated revokes the entire
     session it belongs to, rejects the request with a distinct error code,
     and writes a security event with the token's session id and the
     presenting IP.
   - A refresh token presented more than 30 days after issue is expired and
     rejected without revoking the session.

4. **Session management**
   - An end user lists their active sessions (device label, IP, created,
     last used, current-session marker) and ends any of them.
   - A security admin lists and ends any user's sessions, and can end all
     sessions of a user in one call.
   - Ending a session invalidates its refresh token immediately; access
     tokens already issued stay valid until they expire (at most 15 minutes).

5. **Limits**
   - A user may hold at most 10 active sessions; signing in past the limit
     ends the least recently used session.

## Non-functional requirements
- The exchange endpoint handles 500 requests per second with a 99th
  percentile under 100 ms.
- Rotation is atomic: two concurrent exchanges of the same token result in
  exactly one success and one reuse detection.
- Security events are retained for one year.

## Out of scope
- Multi-factor authentication.
- Device fingerprinting beyond the client-supplied label.
- Access-token revocation lists.

## Acceptance criteria
- Exchange once: new pair returned, old token rejected on second use and the
  session is revoked.
- Concurrent double exchange: one succeeds, one is flagged as reuse, session
  revoked, one security event written.
- Ending a session from the user's list makes the next exchange on that
  session fail.
- An 11th sign-in ends the least recently used session, leaving exactly 10.

epics.title: Token issuance and sessions
epics.description: Issue access/refresh token pairs on sign-in and record a session for each sign-in.

user_stories.title: Receive token pair on sign-in
user_stories.narrative: As an end user, I want to receive an access token and a refresh token when I sign in, so that I can keep using apps without re-login.

specs.title: Token pair issue
specs.description: On sign-in, issue a 15-minute access token and a 30-day opaque refresh token; store only a hash of the refresh token.

tasks.title: Generate opaque refresh token
tasks.description: Generate refresh tokens from a cryptographically secure source with at least 256 bits of entropy.

acceptance_criteria.text: Refresh token has at least 256 bits of entropy
acceptance_criteria.when: a refresh token is generated
acceptance_criteria.then: it is an opaque random string encoding at least 256 bits

tasks.title: Store refresh token hash only
tasks.description: Persist a hash of the refresh token for lookup and comparison; never persist the plaintext token.

acceptance_criteria.when: a refresh token is issued and the datastore is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: the plaintext token appears nowhere and only its hash is stored

tasks.confidence_note: BRD says only a hash is stored but does not name the hash algorithm; assumed a fast one-way hash (e.g. SHA-256) is adequate since tokens are high-entropy.

tasks.title: Issue token pair on sign-in
tasks.description: On successful sign-in return an access token valid 15 minutes and a refresh token valid 30 days.

acceptance_criteria.when: a user signs in successfully
acceptance_criteria.then: the response contains an access token expiring in 15 minutes and a refresh token expiring in 30 days

specs.title: Session record
specs.description: Create a session record at sign-in holding device label, IP, created time and last-used time.

tasks.title: Create session on sign-in
tasks.description: Persist a session with a stable id, client-supplied device label, IP, created time and last-used time, and link the first refresh token to it.

acceptance_criteria.when: a user signs in with a device label from an IP
acceptance_criteria.then: a session exists with that device label, IP, created time and last-used time set

epics.title: Rotation and reuse detection
epics.description: Make refresh tokens single-use, rotate them atomically, and revoke the session on reuse.

user_stories.title: Rotate refresh token on exchange
user_stories.narrative: As a client application, I want to exchange a refresh token for a new pair, so that the user stays signed in with single-use tokens.

specs.title: Rotation exchange
specs.description: Exchange endpoint validates the presented token, marks it used, issues a new access token and new refresh token in the same session, and updates last-used time.

tasks.title: Exchange refresh token for new pair
tasks.description: Validate the presented token, mark it used, and return a new access token and new refresh token bound to the same session id.

acceptance_criteria.text: New pair returned, old token used
acceptance_criteria.when: a valid refresh token is exchanged once
acceptance_criteria.then: a new access token and new refresh token are returned and the old token is marked used

acceptance_criteria.when: a token is rotated
acceptance_criteria.then: the new token belongs to the same session id

tasks.title: Update session last-used time
tasks.description: Set the session last-used time on every successful exchange.

acceptance_criteria.when: an exchange succeeds
acceptance_criteria.then: the session last-used time equals the exchange time

tasks.title: Make rotation atomic
tasks.description: Mark-as-used must be a single atomic conditional operation so concurrent exchanges of one token yield exactly one success.

acceptance_criteria.when: two exchanges of the same token run concurrently
acceptance_criteria.then: exactly one succeeds and the other is treated as reuse

specs.title: Exchange performance
specs.description: Exchange endpoint meets the stated throughput and latency target.

tasks.title: Verify exchange load target
tasks.description: Load-test the exchange endpoint at 500 requests per second and measure latency.

acceptance_criteria.when: the endpoint is loaded at 500 requests per second
acceptance_criteria.then: 99th percentile latency is under 100 ms

user_stories.title: Detect refresh token reuse
user_stories.narrative: As a security admin, I want reuse of a rotated token to revoke the whole session, so that a leaked token is useless after its first use.

specs.title: Reuse handling
specs.description: Detect presentation of an already-used token, revoke its session, reject with a distinct error, and record a security event.

tasks.title: Revoke session on reuse
tasks.description: When an already-rotated token is presented, revoke the owning session and reject the request with a distinct error code.

acceptance_criteria.when: an already-rotated refresh token is presented
acceptance_criteria.then: the session is revoked and the request is rejected with the distinct reuse error code

acceptance_criteria.when: the session was revoked by reuse and its latest refresh token is then presented
acceptance_criteria.then: the exchange is rejected

tasks.confidence_note: BRD requires a 'distinct error code' but does not define its value or HTTP status; assumed a dedicated code (e.g. token_reuse_detected) different from expired/invalid.

tasks.title: Write reuse security event
tasks.description: On reuse, write a security event with the session id and presenting IP.

acceptance_criteria.when: reuse is detected
acceptance_criteria.then: one security event is stored with the session id and presenting IP

tasks.title: Retain security events one year
tasks.description: Apply a one-year retention policy to security events.

acceptance_criteria.when: a security event is older than one year
acceptance_criteria.then: it may be purged, and events younger than one year are never purged

tasks.title: Reject expired token without revoking
tasks.description: Reject tokens presented more than 30 days after issue as expired, leaving the session intact.

acceptance_criteria.when: a refresh token is presented more than 30 days after issue
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is rejected as expired and the session is not revoked

epics.title: Session management and limits
epics.description: Let users and security admins list and end sessions, and cap active sessions per user.

user_stories.title: End user manages own sessions
user_stories.narrative: As an end user, I want to list and end my sessions, so that I can cut off devices I no longer trust.

specs.title: User session API
specs.description: Authenticated endpoints to list the caller's active sessions and end one.

tasks.title: List own active sessions
tasks.description: Return the caller's active sessions with device label, IP, created, last used and a current-session marker.

acceptance_criteria.when: a user requests their sessions
acceptance_criteria.then: each active session shows device label, IP, created, last used, and exactly one is marked current

tasks.confidence_note: BRD does not say how the current session is identified; assumed from the session id carried by the caller's access token.

tasks.title: End own session
tasks.description: Revoke a chosen session of the caller, invalidating its refresh token immediately.

acceptance_criteria.when: a user ends a session from their list and its refresh token is then exchanged
acceptance_criteria.then: the exchange fails

acceptance_criteria.when: a session is ended and an already-issued access token is used within its 15 minutes
acceptance_criteria.then: the access token is still accepted

user_stories.title: Admin revokes user sessions
user_stories.narrative: As a security admin, I want to list and end any user's sessions, so that I can respond to an incident.

specs.title: Admin session API
specs.description: Admin-only endpoints to list a user's sessions, end one, or end all.

tasks.title: Enforce security admin authorization
tasks.description: Restrict admin session endpoints to callers holding the security admin role, as asserted by a role claim in the access token.

acceptance_criteria.when: a caller without the security admin role calls an admin session endpoint
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is rejected as forbidden

tasks.title: Admin list and end user sessions
tasks.description: Let a security admin list any user's sessions and end any single session.

acceptance_criteria.when: an admin requests another user's sessions
acceptance_criteria.then: that user's active sessions are returned

acceptance_criteria.when: an admin ends one of that user's sessions
acceptance_criteria.then: its refresh token is rejected on the next exchange

tasks.title: End all sessions of a user
tasks.description: Provide a single call that revokes every active session of a given user.

acceptance_criteria.when: an admin ends all sessions of a user in one call
acceptance_criteria.then: every session of that user is revoked and none can be exchanged

specs.confidence_note: Endpoint shape is not specified; assumed mirrors of the user endpoints keyed by user id.

user_stories.confidence_note: BRD names the security admin role but not how admin rights are granted or checked.

user_stories.title: Cap active sessions per user
user_stories.narrative: As a security admin, I want each user limited to 10 active sessions, so that stale sessions do not accumulate.

specs.title: Session limit
specs.description: On sign-in, if the user already holds 10 active sessions, end the least recently used one.

tasks.title: Evict LRU session at limit
tasks.description: At sign-in, when the user has 10 active sessions, revoke the session with the oldest last-used time before creating the new one.

acceptance_criteria.when: a user with 10 active sessions signs in an 11th time
acceptance_criteria.then: the least recently used session is ended and exactly 10 active sessions remain
